candidates.label: YCN16-C1
candidates.title: setRatio inclusive-vs-exclusive doc/code deviation (Balancer + Uniboost debt hooks)
candidates.rootCause: setRatio guards `if (newRatio > MAX_RATIO) revert` (inclusive, admits newRatio==MAX_RATIO=50) while NatSpec/story-030 documents an EXCLUSIVE cap ('strictly < MAX_RATIO', 'max settable MAX_RATIO-1'). DEFAULT_RATIO=50 == MAX_RATIO, so the deployed default already contradicts the stale NatSpec. Commit 924b188 raised DEFAULT_RATIO 30->50 without syncing the guard or the doc, so CODE is authoritative and the NatSpec is stale.
corroboratedBy: symbolic check_setRatioInclusiveBound (Uniboost [0,50] proven exhaustive over uint8)
candidates.impactSummary: Cosmetic. Ratio ceiling is 50% inclusive vs documented 49%; both far below 100%, protocol heavily over-backed either way. No unbacked mint, no security consequence. Owner-only setter (Law 3 trusted). Fix is doc-align (or change guard to >=). NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook is EXCLUDED — its inclusive [0,200] NatSpec is self-consistent (story-035).
candidates.preservedDetails: F-16-01 has the fullest spec-source citation and authoritative-source reasoning; keep it as primary.
candidates.keepSeparateNote: This is the Balancer/Uniboost pair only. NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook ratio>100 over-mint is a DIFFERENT concern (YCN16-C6 / DEDUP-001), not this doc bug.

candidates.label: YCN16-C2
candidates.title: Uniboost/BalancerPoolerV2 _dispatch does not enforce hookTypeId (fail-open to under-accrual)
candidates.rootCause: Unlike the two NudgeRatchet variants (which fail-CLOSED via a hookTypeId()==literal require), Uniboost._dispatch and BalancerPoolerV2._dispatch perform NO hook-type validation. If the owner wires DefaultDispatchHook / a wrong hook (or never wires the real one), dispatch still moves value while accruing ZERO phUSD debt. Symmetric enforcement is not even expressible: the Uniboost/Balancer debt hooks expose no hookTypeId() function.
corroboratedBy: faithfulness story-037-asymmetry confirmation (INTENTIONAL per stories, not a deviation)
candidates.impactSummary: Fail-OPEN direction is UNDER-accrual: fewer phUSD minted than backing moved => protocol OVER-backed, never unbacked. Safe direction; breaks debt bookkeeping silently. Owner-configuration-gated footgun, non-catastrophic. Honest severity Low.
candidates.keepSeparateNote: DISTINCT from Q-08 (BalancerPoolerV2 wont-fix). L-09 is the per-dispatcher missing-hookTypeId-enforcement footgun; do not collapse into Q-08.

candidates.label: YCN16-C3
candidates.title: MultiPooler batch: external-call-in-loop + same-pool in-batch floor staleness
candidates.rootCause: MultiPooler.pool(PoolCall[]) forwards one Uniboost.pool per row in an all-or-nothing loop, gated onlyPooler (trusted keeper). If two rows target the same Uniboost/pool, row 1's swaps move AMM reserves so row 2's operator-precomputed minPairOut/minTargetOut floors are stale (worse execution for row 2, bounded by its own floors). MultiPooler holds no funds and has no shared mutable state; each Uniboost.pool is individually nonReentrant.
candidates.impactSummary: At worst a self-DoS (batch reverts on unmet floor) or mildly worse LP execution for a duplicated pool. Keeper self-inflicted / MEV-adjacent, not reachable by an unprivileged actor. Low. (STATIC-021 BatchPooled-event-after-loop is benign and folded here.)

candidates.label: YCN16-C4
candidates.title: Uniboost buy-and-pool spot-swap sandwich MEV (keeper-gated)
candidates.rootCause: Uniboost.pool() executes two spot swaps (prime->pair, ~half pair->target) then addLiquidity on a UniV2 pool with addLiquidity min amounts hardcoded 0 — classic sandwichable buy-and-pool. Mitigated: onlyAuthorizedPooler (keeper), keeper-supplied minPairOut/minTargetOut/minLP slippage floors bound the outcome. Deadline is block.timestamp (no forward deadline, zero MEV/stale-tx protection).
corroboratedBy: STATIC-011 (unchecked swap returns — cleared via CODE-005; amounts re-read by balanceOf + min-out floors)
candidates.impactSummary: Sandwich-exposed but bounded by keeper floors; minLP post-check reverts a manipulated add. amountIn param is MEV-neutral-to-beneficial. Do not re-escalate above Low without a new exploit path (memory: run-13/14).

candidates.label: YCN16-C5
candidates.title: NudgeRatchetDelayRelease pause does not freeze already-held custody
candidates.rootCause: release() carries only onlyReleaser+nonReentrant and rescueERC20() only onlyOwner — neither has whenNotPaused. Pausing the dispatcher freezes NEW dispatch (inflow) but does NOT freeze custody: a releaser can still move held USDC to batchMinter and the owner can still rescue during a pause. Documented intentional (escape hatch must work during pause).
candidates.impactSummary: Low operational footgun — a pause invoked to stop backing egress during an incident would not stop release(); trusted releaser/owner only (Law 3).

candidates.label: YCN16-C6
candidates.title: phUSD debt/backing decoupling + ratio>100 over-mint on NudgeRatchet hook (external-backing boundary)
candidates.rootCause: Two facets of the same external-backing assumption: (a) NudgeRatchetMintDebtHook permits ratio up to MAX_RATIO=200, so pull() can mint up to 2x the dispatched USDC as phUSD (intended 'nudge reward' over-issuance, owner knob, NatSpec-documented); (b) NudgeRatchetDelayRelease decouples debt-accrual (dispatch time, phUSD realisable via pull()) from USDC custody (held until release()), and rescueERC20 can pull the held _token. Whether phUSD is under-backed depends entirely on phUSD's external collateral model, which is OUT OF SCOPE (DEDUP-001).
corroboratedBy: symbolic no-over-mint ceiling INCONCLUSIVE (Halmos div-by-100 timeout; overflow reverts under 0.8.20 checked math, manual inspection holds; NOT machine-proven, zero safety weight either way)
candidates.impactSummary: Backing is conserved on-chain (release only relocates existing USDC); the only ways to move it are onlyReleaser release() and onlyOwner rescueERC20 — both trusted (Law 3). No unprivileged actor can create unbacked phUSD. Reduces to the DEDUP-001 external-backing question. Routed for sanitizer reconciliation against DEDUP-001; a VISIBLE spec-conformance/carryover record (Law-1 recall), not a silent drop.
candidates.keepSeparateNote: KEEP SEPARATE from Q-11 (YCN16-C7, the in-contract bal>=amount tripwire). Do NOT collapse the external-backing model into the in-contract tripwire — different root causes, different mitigations.

This is the in-contract tripwire concern, distinct from the external-backing model.
